name: DS1307 real-time clock
description: Maxim DS1307 I2C real-time clock with its 32.768 kHz crystal: time and date in BCD with 12/24-hour modes, the clock-halt bit (set on a new part: the time stands until it is cleared), a square-wave output (1 Hz, 4.096, 8.192, 32.768 kHz) or OUT level on SQW/OUT, and 56 bytes of battery-backed RAM.

pins.name: X1
pins.doc: 32.768 kHz crystal (the crystal is part of the model)

pins.name: X2
pins.doc: 32.768 kHz crystal (the crystal is part of the model)

pins.name: SQW
pins.doc: Square wave or OUT level, open drain (needs a pull-up)

drift_ppm.doc: The crystal's rate off true, ppm (a 20 ppm crystal is about 1.7 s a day)

start.doc: Date and time a battery kept the clock running at, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS; empty for a new part, its oscillator halted

functional.claims: I2C at 0x68 with user buffers refreshed at each START and at the pointer's wrap; 64 registers wrapping from 3Fh; BCD time and date with 12/24-hour modes and a user day of the week; CH halting the oscillator (set on a new part); the countdown chain reset by a seconds write; the rate off by drift_ppm; the square wave (1 Hz to 32.768 kHz) or OUT on SQW/OUT while wired; 56 bytes of RAM; no answer below VPF (3.75 V).
omissions: the battery (VBAT) switchover and timekeeping on battery
the crystal's frequency against temperature and load capacitance (the drift is a parameter)
the 1 Hz square wave's phase against the seconds
